fields.title: Nothing checks that a running service reports its commit

sections.What it checks:
* [std-DEPLOY.ONCE](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/64704ade123e06dc96422bf6d1d2d21019d3c37f/examples/engineering/standards/common/deployment.md#once-the-artefact-is-built-once) says an artefact "**MUST** record the commit it was built from, so a running
  version identifies the change it came from".
sections.How it works:
Nothing runs. The check this rule needs is a step at the end of each deployment. It requests the service's health endpoint and compares the commit it reports with the commit the pipeline built:

```sh
test "$(curl -fsS "$SERVICE_URL/health" | jq -r .commit)" = "$BUILD_COMMIT"
```

The step fails the deployment where the two differ, or where the endpoint reports no commit. It runs per deployment. A pre-commit check or a Claude Code hook sees only the source, and cannot tell what a running service reports.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
A reviewer reading the health handler is the only thing that notices a missing commit today.

The standard names no endpoint and no field, so the check assumes `/health` and `commit`. The other rules under [std-DEPLOY.ONCE](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/64704ade123e06dc96422bf6d1d2d21019d3c37f/examples/engineering/standards/common/deployment.md#once-the-artefact-is-built-once) go unchecked:

* the pipeline builds once and promotes that build
* the deployment record names the artefact, the change and the approval
* nothing deploys an artefact built outside the pipeline
